expression_comparison.chosen_because: The edge is BoC policy restraint underpriced versus the Fed, not a USD hike that was >90% priced nor an RBA path already in 99th-percentile ACGBs. CA-US 2Y is the tenor and market that holds that gap, is historically extreme on both 1y and 5y windows, and pays the US-Canada pickup while waiting. Outright CAN 2Y chases a 1y extreme; CAN 2s10s is already a 1y flattening extreme; USDCAD is a dirtier oil/risk residual with the wrong carry. No vol surface is in the packet.

considered_rates.assessment: Pay CAN 2Y at 3.35% owns the BoC reaction function directly. It is only the 60.5th percentile on a 5y window versus UST 2Y at the 83.9th and ACGB 2Y at the 99.96th, so Canada is the least stretched front end in the packet on a long window. Rejected as the primary expression because the 1y percentile is already 99.0 with +38bp/1m and +60bp/3m, so an outright short fights a 1y extreme instead of the cleaner cross-market discrepancy, and it pays 3.35% rather than harvesting the US-Canada pickup.

A hawkish bear-flattener is the textbook front-end-underpriced trade, but CAN 2s10s is already 57bp at the 0.79th 1y percentile (-18bp/1m) and CAN 5s10s is at the 0.20th. Chasing a 1y curve extreme is a crowded expression of tightness that is already in the Canadian curve, not the gap versus the Fed. UST 2s10s is likewise at the 1.39th 1y percentile, so US curve is not a clean delayed-easing fade either.

This is the discrepancy. CA-US 2Y -139bp is the 4.76th 1y and 4.67th 5y percentile, -17bp/1m and -12bp/5d. It isolates CAD policy that is still priced as if BoC can stay 139bp easier after a delivered Fed hike, 3% headline, and an energy-pass-through minute. Receiving UST 2Y versus paying CAN 2Y is carry-positive at the packet spread while waiting for compression. CA-US 5Y at -122bp is even more extreme on 1y (0.20th) but 2Y is closer to the reaction function. AU-US 2Y at +40.5bp (89th 5y) shows RBA tightness is already priced; NZ RV is unavailable.

considered_spot.assessment: Short USDCAD would own hawk CAD in the currency the remit cares about. Spot is 1.39953, 70.8th 1y / 86.2nd 5y, so CAD is cheap-ish but not the 4.7th-percentile extreme the rates spread is. Spot is dirtied by the Saudi oil-workaround (CAD terms-of-trade), energy risk-off, and the post-FOMC 5d USDCAD +1.30%. Carry would be negative because CAD 2Y is 139bp through UST 2Y. Rates own the mispricing; spot does not.

trade.thesis: The hawk residual after a fully priced Fed 25bp hike is not more UST duration at a 99th-percentile 1y yield; it is the central bank that still treats energy as look-through while its 2Y sits 139bp through Treasuries. Canada August headline CPI is 3% with BoC minutes flagging higher energy pass-through, global energy shock absorbers are weakening, and the ECB has already hiked on energy. CA-US 2Y at -139bp is in the 4.8th percentile over 1y and the 4.7th over 5y, while CAN 2Y is only the 60.5th percentile on a 5y window versus UST 2Y at the 83.9th. That is policy restraint underpriced in CAD, not a one-and-done USD story.
